answer: Assign each account one cedar sapling planted on a distinct terrace of a shared hillside grove near the tundra edge, marked with a carved tag bearing a unique code. Each season, the owner measures the sapling's height and girth beside the terrace number stone and submits a photo with a dated card; two nearby grove keepers countersign the reading. A Sybil farm would need a separate real sapling, its own terrace, and years of slow cedar growth per identity, so mass-producing fake accounts becomes expensive, time-consuming, and obvious when heights cluster impossibly or terraces repeat.
